title: Trend of Migrant Workers Staying in Dormitories Seeking Mental Healthcare
what_it_is: Trend of Migrant Workers Staying in Dormitories Seeking Mental Healthcare

sections.label: Work permit holders admitted to IMH
sections.summary: Between January and September 2021, 98 work permit holders were admitted to IMH, lower than the same period in 2020 but higher than 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Between January and September 2021, 98 work permit holders were admitted to IMH.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This was lower as compared to the same period in 2020, but was higher as compared to 2019, during the pre-COVID-19 era.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: An earlier study, which was conducted by Yale-NUS on migrant workers' mental health from June to October 2020, showed no notable difference in stress, anxiety and depression levels amongst locals and migrant workers, although there were indications of higher levels of stress amongst migrant workers with movement restrictions.

sections.label: Dormitory residents' recreation centre visits
sections.summary: Since August last year dormitory residents have been allowed to visit recreation centres, with frequency recently increased to three times a week from once a week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since August last year, we have allowed dormitory residents to visit recreation centres, or RCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We recently increased the frequency of RC visits to thrice or three times a week, up from once a week.

sections.label: Planning easing of restrictions
sections.summary: Easing of restrictions was planned as early as December last year, about a month after the DAWN task force was formed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: They are also at the back of — well, not at the back of our minds, but on an almost daily basis, we contemplate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We planned for the easing of the restrictions as early as December last year; this was about a month after we formed the DAWN task force.

sections.label: Pilot allowing 500 to go out
sections.summary: A pilot in mid-September allowed 500 to go out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With that, we took on that pilot in mid-September to allow 500 to go out.

sections.label: Ramping up from 500 to 3,000
sections.summary: After ascertaining the visit was safe and needs were addressed, the number was increased sixfold from 500 to 3,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: When we were able to ascertain that the entire visit was safe, that we were able to adequately address the physical, mental and social needs; on top of that, keep them medically well-protected, we then ramped up from 500, increasing it sixfold to 3,000.

sections.label: Opening up in new normal
sections.summary: The plan in the coming weeks and months, as Singapore moves to a new normal, is not to restrict but to open up more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The plan, hopefully, in the ensuing weeks and months ahead, is that as we move to this new normal, is not to restrict but to open up even more.
